title: A commit whose index undoes the branch's own earlier commits is caught
why: Lane red-run-pre-push's finding: a branch commit that undoes the branch's own earlier commits nets to no change against the base, so PR-mode check_silent_undo and #2136 miss it; only the --history audit reads it, and it exits 0 (lane silent-undo-checks-pr-base, 11:05 CST Nov 8). Open design question: a commit-time guard (the index base is not HEAD's tree) or a reversal read of the branch's own commits in check_silent_undo. Red cases first either way.
note: Lane 11:07 CST Nov 8: a Plan agent picks the home; red cases follow.
